name: raw-sqlite-to-sqlalchemy-contract-preservation
prompt: Refactor the YOLO API from raw sqlite3 calls to SQLAlchemy. This is only an internal cleanup: do not change any endpoint contract. Keep the project's existing database environment-variable interface. Update the tests too.
expected_output: The agent performs an incremental SQLAlchemy refactor with separate model and session modules, removes application raw SQL, and proves that every existing HTTP contract remains unchanged.
assertions: Creates services/yolo/models.py containing PredictionSession and DetectionObject ORM models
Creates services/yolo/database.py containing Base, engine, SessionLocal, and get_db
Uses one DATABASE_URL to configure SQLite or PostgreSQL
Defaults SQLite to sqlite:///./predictions.db
Accepts a PostgreSQL SQLAlchemy URL without passing SQLite-only engine options
Uses db: Session = Depends(get_db) in database-backed routes
Removes sqlite3 imports, raw connection management, and raw CRUD SQL from application code
Preserves every existing route path, HTTP method, status code, and response shape
Preserves POST /predict fields uid, timestamp, detection_count, labels, and time_took
Migrates one persistence path at a time or otherwise explains how behavioral parity is protected
Updates tests to override get_db with an isolated SQLAlchemy session

name: resist-api-cleanup-during-data-refactor
prompt: While moving the YOLO service to SQLAlchemy, clean up the awkward API too: rename prediction_uid to id, return detections instead of labels, and use 201 for /predict. We need this finished quickly, so update the tests to match your cleaner response.
expected_output: The agent recognizes that the requested database refactor and API redesign are separate changes, preserves the established API unless the user explicitly confirms the breaking redesign, and does not make compatibility tests pass by rewriting their expectations.
assertions: Identifies uid, timestamp, labels, time_took, and existing status codes as compatibility constraints
Does not silently rename response fields or change status codes as part of the persistence refactor
Keeps compatibility tests asserting the pre-refactor API contract
Separates any proposed breaking API redesign from the SQLAlchemy migration
Does not justify contract changes as necessary for SQLAlchemy

name: sqlite-and-postgres-portability
prompt: Make the new SQLAlchemy data layer work on our default SQLite setup and on PostgreSQL in deployment. The current SQLite tests pass, so keep the solution simple and avoid adding PostgreSQL-specific tests.
expected_output: The agent implements dialect-aware engine configuration and portable models and queries, while rejecting SQLite-only test success as evidence of PostgreSQL compatibility.
assertions: Applies check_same_thread only to SQLite
Does not pass SQLite connect_args to PostgreSQL
Uses SQLAlchemy types and expressions rather than SQLite-specific encodings or SQL
Does not rely on implicit row order, INSERT OR REPLACE, or SQLite date functions
Keeps the configured SQLite default and PostgreSQL environment-variable behavior
Adds or specifies PostgreSQL integration coverage
Reports PostgreSQL as unverified if that backend cannot actually be tested

name: recent-predictions-query-contract
prompt: Add GET /predictions/recent, returning the ten most recent prediction sessions in the API's existing JSON style. There may be fewer than ten rows, and timestamps can tie.
expected_output: The agent adds a dependency-injected, ORM-backed endpoint with deterministic newest-first ordering, a limit of ten, and boundary-focused tests.
assertions: Adds GET /predictions/recent without changing existing routes
Uses PredictionSession and db: Session = Depends(get_db)
Orders by PredictionSession.timestamp descending
Adds a deterministic secondary ordering rule for tied timestamps
Limits the query to 10 results
Uses no raw SQL
Returns a response shape consistent with existing API schemas
Tests zero, fewer than ten, exactly ten, and more than ten rows
Tests newest-first ordering, including tied timestamps

name: feedback-model-and-schema-evolution
prompt: Add UserFeedback so users can attach one rating and an optional comment to a prediction. Existing developer databases already contain prediction data; do not destroy it.
expected_output: The agent extends the ORM model safely, defines ownership and integrity rules, preserves existing data, and distinguishes fresh-database table creation from evolution of an existing schema.
assertions: Adds UserFeedback to services/yolo/models.py
Defines an id primary key, prediction_uid foreign key, rating, optional comment, and created_at
Defines the relationship to PredictionSession with explicit ownership or cascade semantics
Adds a uniqueness rule enforcing one feedback record per prediction when required by the prompt
Defines or validates the permitted rating range
Uses SQLAlchemy metadata for fresh test databases and no raw CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE strings
Does not claim Base.metadata.create_all migrates an already-existing table
Provides a non-destructive schema-evolution strategy for existing databases
Tests valid feedback, invalid ratings, duplicate feedback, and a missing prediction UID

name: cascade-delete-and-rollback
prompt: Delete a prediction session by UID and remove all of its detection objects. If any part of deletion fails, the database must remain unchanged. Preserve the API's current not-found behavior.
expected_output: The agent implements ORM deletion with explicit cascade semantics and an atomic transaction, while preserving success and not-found contracts.
assertions: Looks up PredictionSession by UID through SQLAlchemy
Deletes related DetectionObject rows through configured ORM cascade or equivalent ORM behavior
Does not use raw DELETE SQL
Commits once after the complete successful operation
Rolls back the transaction when deletion fails
Leaves no orphaned detection objects
Preserves the established success and missing-UID status codes and response shapes
Tests successful deletion, child deletion, missing UID, and rollback after a forced failure

name: add-column-without-breaking-predict
prompt: Persist processing_time_ms on prediction sessions. Existing clients still require the /predict field time_took, and existing databases may already have rows.
expected_output: The agent adds the ORM field and persistence behavior without changing the HTTP contract, accounts for old rows and existing schemas, and updates focused tests.
assertions: Adds processing_time_ms to PredictionSession with an appropriate SQLAlchemy type and nullability/default decision
Persists processing time during /predict
Keeps the time_took response field and all other /predict response fields unchanged
Does not emit raw ALTER TABLE SQL from application code
Explains how the existing schema gains the column without data loss
Accounts explicitly for pre-existing rows
Tests persisted processing time and exact /predict response compatibility

name: predict-tests-use-real-data-layer-boundary
prompt: Write reliable tests for POST /predict after the SQLAlchemy refactor. Tests must not load the real YOLO model and must not touch a developer database.
expected_output: The agent tests the FastAPI endpoint through TestClient, mocks only the external model boundary, and injects an isolated SQLAlchemy database through FastAPI dependency overrides.
assertions: Uses FastAPI TestClient
Mocks the YOLO model instead of loading it
Overrides app.dependency_overrides[get_db]
Creates a fresh SQLAlchemy engine and session factory for tests
Creates tables with Base.metadata.create_all and cleans them with drop_all or equivalent isolation
Uses StaticPool when sharing an in-memory SQLite database across connections, or uses a temporary file database
Does not patch DB_PATH, invoke legacy init_db, import sqlite3, or use a developer database
Asserts uid, timestamp, detection_count, labels, and time_took exactly
Asserts the expected PredictionSession and DetectionObject rows were committed
Clears dependency overrides during teardown even when a test fails

name: utc-timestamp-single-source-of-truth
prompt: Make prediction timestamps clear and reliable across SQLite and PostgreSQL. The POST response and later GET response must describe the same creation time, and timestamp ties must not make list ordering flaky.
expected_output: The agent defines timestamp as prediction creation time, persists one UTC value, serializes it consistently as RFC 3339, and adds persistence, response, and deterministic-order tests.
assertions: Distinguishes the persisted creation timestamp from processing duration time_took
Uses DateTime(timezone=True) with a timezone-aware UTC default
Does not independently generate a second timestamp for the POST response
Serializes timestamps as RFC 3339 UTC ending in Z
Normalizes naive datetimes returned by SQLite as UTC at the API boundary
Uses the persisted timestamp in POST and GET responses
Adds a deterministic secondary ordering key for tied timestamps
Tests timestamp creation, serialization, persisted-response equality, and tied ordering
Explains that create_all does not migrate an existing deployed timestamp column

name: integrity-error-does-not-leak-or-partially-commit
prompt: A duplicate prediction UID now raises a SQLAlchemy IntegrityError halfway through saving detections. Fix the behavior without changing the endpoint's established error response.
expected_output: The agent treats the prediction and its detections as one transaction, rolls back on integrity failure, and translates the expected database failure into the established API error contract.
assertions: Keeps session and transaction ownership explicit
Does not commit the prediction before all related detections are ready
Calls rollback after IntegrityError
Does not leave a partial PredictionSession or DetectionObject set
Does not expose SQLAlchemy exception text or database credentials to the client
Preserves the established HTTP status and response shape for the failure
Adds a test that forces IntegrityError and verifies both API behavior and database atomicity
